# Overview

**Module 4: UMI**

Every read in a UMI family descends from one original DNA molecule with one true repeat length, so the spread of lengths within a family is PCR slippage plus sequencing error. This module turns reads into molecules:

1. The UMI is the sequence between `r params$umi_flank_5` (5') and `r params$umi_flank_3` (3'), located on the strand-corrected read with up to `r params$umi_flank_max_mismatch` edits (an exact match is used where there is one), and must be `r params$umi_len_min`–`r params$umi_len_max` bases long
2. UMIs are clustered per sample with the directional rule at edit distance `r params$umi_cluster_max_dist`: a UMI joins a neighbour that has at least twice its reads (minus one)
3. Each UMI family (all reads whose UMIs clustered together) is one molecule. Repeat length plays no part in forming molecules: PCR slippage and deletion can make reads of one molecule differ by tens of units, which is the error collapsing is meant to remove, so length cannot be used to decide which reads belong together. Nothing is assumed about how many alleles or clones a sample has
4. Molecules with fewer than `r params$umi_min_reads` reads are dropped, and every measure is collapsed to one length per molecule with **`r params$umi_collapse_stat`**`r if (params$umi_collapse_stat == "top_cluster") sprintf(" (the median of the highest window of half-width %g + %g × length holding at least %d reads%s)", params$umi_top_cluster_w, params$umi_top_cluster_wfrac, params$umi_top_cluster_k, if (params$umi_top_cluster_min_share > 0) sprintf(" and at least %s of the molecule's reads", percent(params$umi_top_cluster_min_share)) else "") else ""`. A length halfway between two whole units goes to the one more of the molecule's reads sit on. Other length rules are compared in *Choosing a molecule's length*
5. Molecules where at least `r percent(params$umi_long_read_share)` of the reads are at least `r params$umi_long_read_units` units longer than the molecule itself are flagged`r if (isTRUE(params$umi_long_read_filter)) " and dropped" else " (and kept, as umi_long_read_filter = FALSE)"`: such a molecule most likely came from a longer template whose reads were mostly shortened in PCR, so its length is too short. See *Molecules built from a longer template*

Modules 6 and 7 then report every result twice: per read and per molecule.

**Outputs:**

- `04_umi/umi.xlsx` – extraction, clustering and molecule summaries per sample
- `04_umi/molecules/{sample}.tsv.gz` – one row per molecule with its length for every measure
- `module_data/04_umi.RData` – read-to-molecule map and molecule lengths

# UMI extraction

```{r extract}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
safe_load_module(file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "02_alignment.RData"), 2)
safe_load_module(file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "03_repeat_detection.RData"), 3)
primary <- module3_output$primary; measures <- module3_output$measures
ref1 <- names(module2_output$refs)[1]
aln <- module2_output$alignments[[ref1]][, .(file_stem, qname, query_sequence)]
rm(module2_output); invisible(gc())
per_sample <- split(aln, aln$file_stem)
extracted <- apply_fn(names(per_sample), function(s) {
  a <- per_sample[[s]]
  cbind(a[, .(file_stem, qname)], extract_umis(a$query_sequence, params$umi_flank_5, params$umi_flank_3,
                                                params$umi_flank_max_mismatch, params$umi_search_window,
                                                params$umi_len_min, params$umi_len_max))
})
umi_reads <- rbindlist(extracted); rm(extracted, per_sample, aln)
timings["Extraction"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
outcome <- umi_reads[, .N, by = .(file_stem, umi_outcome)][, prop := N / sum(N), by = file_stem]
cat(sprintf("UMI extracted from %s of %s reads (%.1f%%).", comma(sum(umi_reads$umi_outcome == "UMI extracted")),
            comma(nrow(umi_reads)), 100 * mean(umi_reads$umi_outcome == "UMI extracted")))
```

## Extraction outcome

Each point is one sample: the share of its reads in each outcome. **No 5' flank** usually means the read was trimmed or truncated before the UMI (check that demultiplexing leaves the 5' flank in the read); **wrong length** UMIs are mostly synthesis or sequencing indels.

```{r outcome_plot, fig.height=5}
outcome[, umi_outcome := factor(umi_outcome, levels = c("UMI extracted", "UMI wrong length or contains N", "no 3' flank", "flanks overlap", "no 5' flank"))]
p_out <- ggplot(outcome, aes(umi_outcome, prop)) + box_points_mean(digits = 1, percent = TRUE) + coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.12))) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads in the sample", title = "UMI extraction outcome, per sample") + theme_bw()
print(p_out); save_plot(p_out, file.path(plots_dir, "extraction_outcome.png"), 9, 5)
```

## UMI length

The length of every UMI found between the flanks, before the length filter, pooled across samples: one bar per length, labelled with its share of UMIs. Teal lengths are accepted (`umi_len_min`–`umi_len_max` = `r params$umi_len_min`–`r params$umi_len_max`), grey are rejected. The designed length should hold nearly all UMIs; one base either side is indels in synthesis or sequencing. Lengths holding under 0.01% of UMIs are grouped at the ends.

```{r umi_length, fig.height=4.5}
lens <- umi_reads[!is.na(umi_length), .N, by = umi_length][, share := N / sum(N)]
keep_len <- lens[share >= 1e-4 | (umi_length >= params$umi_len_min & umi_length <= params$umi_len_max), umi_length]
lo <- min(keep_len); hi <- max(keep_len)
lens[, label := data.table::fifelse(umi_length < lo, paste0("< ", lo, " nt"),
                  data.table::fifelse(umi_length > hi, paste0("> ", hi, " nt"), paste0(umi_length, " nt")))]
lens[, key := pmin(pmax(umi_length, lo - 1), hi + 1)]
lb <- lens[, .(N = sum(N), share = sum(share), accepted = all(umi_length >= params$umi_len_min & umi_length <= params$umi_len_max)), by = .(key, label)][order(key)]
lb[, label := factor(label, levels = rev(label))]
p_len <- ggplot(lb, aes(share, label, fill = accepted)) + geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%s  (%s)", percent(share, 0.01), comma(N))), hjust = -0.05, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#00838f", `FALSE` = "grey65"), labels = c(`TRUE` = "accepted", `FALSE` = "rejected"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(x = "Share of UMIs (number of reads in brackets)", y = "UMI length", title = "UMI length, all samples") + theme_bw()
print(p_len); save_plot(p_len, file.path(plots_dir, "umi_length.png"), 9, max(3, 0.35 * nrow(lb) + 1.5))
```

# Molecules

```{r molecules}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
lengths <- module3_output$lengths
prim <- lengths[measure == primary, .(file_stem, qname, primary = length)]
umi_reads <- prim[umi_reads, on = .(file_stem, qname)]
by_s <- split(umi_reads[!is.na(umi) & !is.na(primary)], by = "file_stem")
len_s <- split(lengths, by = "file_stem")
mols <- apply_fn(names(by_s), function(s) form_molecules(s, by_s[[s]], len_s[[s]][, .(qname, measure, length)], params, primary))
read_map <- rbindlist(lapply(mols, `[[`, "reads"))
molecules <- rbindlist(lapply(mols, `[[`, "molecules"))
molecule_lengths <- rbindlist(lapply(mols, `[[`, "molecule_lengths"))
clustering <- rbindlist(lapply(mols, `[[`, "clustering"))
collapse_compare <- rbindlist(lapply(mols, `[[`, "collapse_compare"))
rm(mols, by_s, len_s)
umi_reads <- read_map[, .(file_stem, qname, umi_group, molecule_id)][umi_reads, on = .(file_stem, qname)]
timings["Clustering and collapse"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
rules_md <- collapse_rules(params)
used_rule_text <- switch(params$umi_collapse_stat,
  top_cluster = sprintf("top_cluster, %d reads%s", params$umi_top_cluster_k,
                        if (params$umi_top_cluster_min_share > 0) sprintf(" and %s", percent(params$umi_top_cluster_min_share)) else ""),
  max_supported = sprintf("longest length on %d reads", params$umi_top_cluster_k), params$umi_collapse_stat)
summary_tab <- molecules[, .(molecules = .N, enough_reads = sum(kept_depth), long_read_flag = sum(long_flag), kept = sum(kept),
                             reads_in_kept = sum(n_reads[kept]), median_reads_per_kept = as.numeric(median(n_reads[kept]))), by = file_stem]
summary_tab <- clustering[, .(file_stem, n_reads_with_umi, distinct_umis, umi_groups, umis_with_neighbour, expected_by_chance)][summary_tab, on = "file_stem"]
dt_full(summary_tab, caption = "UMI clustering and molecules per sample", digits = 2)
```

## Reads per molecule

**How to read this.** A *molecule* is one UMI family: all the reads whose UMIs clustered together, which came from one original DNA molecule. The x-axis is how many reads a molecule received, on a log scale, so that 1, 10 and 100 reads are evenly spaced. **Top panel:** how many molecules received that many reads. **Bottom panel:** how many reads those molecules hold in total (number of molecules × reads each). Teal molecules are kept; grey ones have fewer than `umi_min_reads` = `r params$umi_min_reads` reads and are dropped; orange ones have enough reads but were `r if (isTRUE(params$umi_long_read_filter)) "dropped" else "flagged (not dropped)"` by the long-read check (see *Molecules built from a longer template*). The solid line is the median and the dashed line the mean number of reads per kept molecule, with their values in the subtitle.

**What it shows.** Most molecules are seen only once or twice, but they hold few of the reads; most reads sit in the kept molecules, which are what Modules 5–7 use. Many single-read molecules mean the run was shallow for the number of tagged molecules (each was sampled only once), or that UMIs carrying errors were not merged into their parent.

```{r family_size, fig.height=5.5}
km <- molecules[kept == TRUE, n_reads]
# Log-spaced bins: every count from 1 to 10 gets its own bin, larger counts share
# bins of equal width on the log scale
# (edges halfway between whole counts, so no bin falls between two counts and stays empty)
fs_edges <- unique(c(0.5:10.5, floor(10^seq(log10(11), log10(max(molecules$n_reads, 11) + 1), length.out = 30)) + 0.5))
molecules[, status := factor(ifelse(!kept_depth, "too few reads", ifelse(long_flag, "long-read flag", "kept")), levels = c("too few reads", "long-read flag", "kept"))]
fs <- molecules[, .(molecules = .N, reads = sum(n_reads)), by = .(bin = findInterval(n_reads, fs_edges), status)]
fs[, `:=`(xmin = fs_edges[bin], xmax = fs_edges[bin + 1])]
fs <- melt(fs, id.vars = c("bin", "xmin", "xmax", "status"), measure.vars = c("molecules", "reads"), variable.name = "what", value.name = "n")
fs[, what := factor(what, levels = c("molecules", "reads"), labels = c("Molecules", "Reads in those molecules"))]
# Stack the statuses within each bin
setorder(fs, what, bin, status)
fs[, `:=`(ymax = cumsum(n)), by = .(what, bin)][, ymin := ymax - n]
fs_stats <- data.table(stat = c("median", "mean"), x = c(stats::median(km), mean(km)))
p_fam <- ggplot(fs) + geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = status)) +
  geom_vline(data = fs_stats, aes(xintercept = x, linetype = stat), colour = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~ what, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 5000), labels = comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`too few reads` = "grey65", `long-read flag` = "#e6862e", kept = "#00838f"), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(median = "solid", mean = "dashed"), name = "Kept molecules") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Reads in the molecule (log scale)", y = "Count", title = "Reads per molecule, all samples",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s molecules; %s kept (%.1f%%), holding %.1f%% of the reads\nKept molecules: median %s reads, mean %.1f, middle 50%% %s-%s, middle 80%% %s-%s",
                          comma(nrow(molecules)), comma(length(km)), 100 * length(km) / nrow(molecules),
                          100 * sum(km) / sum(molecules$n_reads), median(km), mean(km),
                          stats::quantile(km, 0.25), stats::quantile(km, 0.75), stats::quantile(km, 0.1), stats::quantile(km, 0.9))) + theme_bw()
print(p_fam); save_plot(p_fam, file.path(plots_dir, "reads_per_molecule.png"), 11, 6.5)
```

### Molecules and depth per sample

**How to read this.** Each point is one sample; the box shows the spread across samples and the red diamond and number the mean. **Left:** how many molecules each sample kept. **Middle:** the median number of reads per kept molecule in that sample. **Right:** the share of the sample's reads that are in kept molecules. The scatter below puts the first two together.

**What it shows.** How evenly the samples were sampled. A sample with few molecules had little input DNA (or few reads); a sample with a low median depth was sequenced too shallowly for its number of molecules, so its molecule lengths rest on fewer reads each; a low share of reads in kept molecules means most of its reads were in molecules too small to keep.

```{r family_size_sample, fig.height=4.5}
ps <- molecules[, .(kept = sum(kept), median_reads = as.numeric(median(n_reads[kept])), reads_in_kept = sum(n_reads[kept]) / sum(n_reads)), by = file_stem]
p_ps1 <- ggplot(ps, aes("", kept)) + box_points_mean(fmt = function(v) comma(round(v))) + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Molecules kept", title = "Molecules kept") + theme_bw()
p_ps2 <- ggplot(ps, aes("", median_reads)) + box_points_mean(digits = 1) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Median reads per kept molecule", title = "Reads per kept molecule") + theme_bw()
p_ps3 <- ggplot(ps, aes("", reads_in_kept)) + box_points_mean(digits = 1, percent = TRUE) + scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads in kept molecules", title = "Reads used") + theme_bw()
p_psb <- patchwork::wrap_plots(p_ps1, p_ps2, p_ps3, nrow = 1)
print(p_psb); save_plot(p_psb, file.path(plots_dir, "molecules_per_sample.png"), 11, 4.5)
```

```{r family_size_scatter, fig.height=5}
p_ps <- ggplot(ps, aes(kept, median_reads)) + geom_point(colour = "#00838f", size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) + scale_y_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200, 500)) +
  labs(x = "Molecules kept (log scale)", y = "Median reads per kept molecule (log scale)", title = "Molecules and depth per sample",
       subtitle = "Each point is one sample") + theme_bw()
print(p_ps); save_plot(p_ps, file.path(plots_dir, "molecules_and_depth.png"), 8, 5)
```

## UMI neighbours against chance

A UMI's **neighbour** is another distinct UMI in the same sample that differs from it by at most `r max(1, params$umi_cluster_max_dist)` edit(s) (a substituted, inserted or deleted base). Two kinds of neighbour exist: copies of a real UMI that picked up an error in PCR or sequencing, which clustering should merge back into their parent, and genuinely different UMIs that happen to be similar by chance, which it should not.

The **expected** share is calculated, not observed: if the sample's *n* distinct UMIs were random sequences of length *L* with no errors, the chance that a given one has a neighbour among the other *n* – 1 is 1 – (1 – *p*)^(*n* – 1), where *p* is the chance that two random *L*-mers differ by at most `r max(1, params$umi_cluster_max_dist)` substitution(s) (for one substitution and *L* = 14, *p* = (1 + 3*L*) / 4^*L* ≈ 1.6 × 10^–7^). The **observed** share is the proportion of the sample's distinct UMIs that actually have a neighbour.

Each pair of points joined by a line is one sample. Observed far above expected means most neighbours are error copies, so clustering is merging errors rather than distinct molecules; observed close to expected would mean there is little to merge and the clustering distance could be lowered.

```{r neighbours, fig.height=5}
nb <- clustering[, .(file_stem, Expected = expected_by_chance / distinct_umis, Observed = umis_with_neighbour / distinct_umis)]
nb_l <- melt(nb, id.vars = "file_stem", variable.name = "what", value.name = "share")
p_nb <- ggplot(nb_l, aes(what, share)) + geom_line(aes(group = file_stem), colour = "grey75") + box_points_mean(digits = 2, percent = TRUE, jitter = 0) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Distinct UMIs with a neighbour", title = "UMI neighbours: observed against chance",
       subtitle = sprintf("Median per sample: %s observed, %s expected by chance", percent(median(nb$Observed), 0.1), percent(median(nb$Expected), 0.01))) + theme_bw()
print(p_nb); save_plot(p_nb, file.path(plots_dir, "umi_neighbours.png"), 7, 5)
```

# What collapsing removes

## Read error within molecules

For every read in a kept molecule, and for every measure (each tract and each combined measure): the read's length minus its molecule's collapsed length. This is the error that collapsing removes. Each read is compared with its own molecule, so nothing is assumed about alleles: it works the same for controls, single-allele samples and samples with several expanded clones.

```{r within_error_data}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
rm_map <- umi_reads[!is.na(molecule_id), .(file_stem, qname, molecule_id)]
wl <- lengths[rm_map, on = .(file_stem, qname), nomatch = NULL]
wl <- molecule_lengths[, .(molecule_id, measure, molecule_length = length)][wl, on = .(molecule_id, measure), nomatch = NULL]
wl[, dev := length - molecule_length]
wl[, measure := factor(measure, levels = measures$measure)]
we_sum <- wl[, .(reads = .N, exact = mean(abs(dev) <= 0.5), below = mean(dev < -0.5), above = mean(dev > 0.5),
                 mean_abs_error = mean(abs(dev)), sd = sd(dev)), by = measure]
# By molecule length: 1-unit bins, or 5-unit bins where a measure spans more than 40 units
wl[, bin_width := { sp <- diff(stats::quantile(molecule_length, c(0.001, 0.999))); if (sp > 40) 5 else 1 }, by = measure]
wl[, length_bin := floor(molecule_length / bin_width) * bin_width]
we_len <- wl[, .(reads = .N, exact = mean(abs(dev) <= 0.5), below = mean(dev < -0.5), above = mean(dev > 0.5),
                 q10 = stats::quantile(dev, 0.10), q25 = stats::quantile(dev, 0.25), median = stats::median(dev),
                 q75 = stats::quantile(dev, 0.75), q90 = stats::quantile(dev, 0.90)), by = .(measure, length_bin)][reads >= 50][order(measure, length_bin)]
dt_compact(we_sum, caption = "Within-molecule read error per measure: share of reads exactly at, below and above their molecule's length", digits = 3)
```

### Error by repeat length

**How to read this.** The x-axis is the molecule's length (its collapsed `r primary` length, in repeat units, e.g. CAG repeats). The y-axis is each read's length **minus** its own molecule's length, in the same units: 0 means the read has the molecule's length; –10 means the read is 10 units shorter than the molecule it came from; +3 means 3 units longer. **Top:** the line is the median read, the dark band holds the middle 50% of reads and the light band the middle 80%. **Bottom:** the share of reads that have exactly their molecule's length. All samples are pooled; lengths with fewer than 50 reads are left out. Each panel is one measure (tract or combined measure).

**What it shows.** How much PCR and sequencing change a read from the molecule it came from, at each length. PCR slippage grows with tract length and mostly loses repeats, so for a CAG tract the bands widen and sit below zero as length increases, and fewer reads are exactly right. At lengths above the common ones, a median well below zero means most of a molecule's reads are much shorter than the length it was given: the length is then being set by a minority of long reads (see *Choosing a molecule's length*).

```{r within_error_length, fig.height=7}
p_wb <- ggplot(we_len, aes(length_bin)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q10, ymax = q90), fill = "#00838f", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), fill = "#00838f", alpha = 0.45) + geom_line(aes(y = median), colour = "#00838f") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") + facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free", nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Read length minus its molecule's length\n(repeat units; below 0 = read shorter)", title = "Within-molecule read error by molecule length") + theme_bw()
p_wx <- ggplot(we_len, aes(length_bin, exact)) + geom_line(colour = "#00838f") + geom_point(colour = "#00838f", size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) + scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Molecule length (repeat units)", y = "Reads exactly at the\nmolecule's length") + theme_bw() + theme(strip.text = element_blank(), strip.background = element_blank())
p_we <- patchwork::wrap_plots(p_wb, p_wx, ncol = 1, heights = c(2, 1))
print(p_we); save_plot(p_we, file.path(plots_dir, "within_molecule_error.png"), max(8, 4 * nrow(measures)), 7)
```

### Error distribution

**How to read this.** Every read in a kept molecule, all samples and lengths pooled, one panel per measure. For each distance *k* on the x-axis (repeat units), the y-axis gives the share of reads that are at least *k* units **shorter** than their molecule (orange) or at least *k* units **longer** (blue). Both start at the share of reads that differ at all and fall as *k* grows; the y-axis is logarithmic, so that the rare large errors can be read alongside the common small ones. The subtitle gives the shares shorter than, equal to and longer than the molecule.

**What it shows.** How far reads stray from their molecule, and in which direction. Read across at, say, 10 units to see what share of reads are off by 10 or more. Where the orange line sits above the blue, PCR loses repeats more often than it gains them (contraction bias). A flat shoulder far out on one line means many reads sit at one particular distance from their molecule, which usually means reads of another allele or molecule in the same UMI family (a PCR chimera or two molecules sharing a UMI), not slippage.

```{r within_error_hist, fig.height=4.5}
wh_max <- wl[, .(kmax = max(1, ceiling(stats::quantile(abs(dev), 0.9999)))), by = measure]
wh <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(wh_max)), function(i) {
  m <- wh_max$measure[i]; d <- wl[measure == m, dev]; n <- length(d)
  k <- unique(round(10^seq(0, log10(wh_max$kmax[i]), length.out = 120)))
  sh <- sort(-d[d < -0.5]); lo <- sort(d[d > 0.5])
  rbind(data.table(measure = m, k = k, share = (length(sh) - findInterval(k - 0.5, sh)) / n, dir = "At least k units shorter"),
        data.table(measure = m, k = k, share = (length(lo) - findInterval(k - 0.5, lo)) / n, dir = "At least k units longer"))
}))
wh <- wh[share > 0]
wh[, measure := factor(measure, levels = measures$measure)]
wh_lab <- we_sum[, .(measure, label = sprintf("Shorter %s, exact %s, longer %s", percent(below, 0.1), percent(exact, 0.1), percent(above, 0.1)))]
p_wh <- ggplot(wh, aes(k, share, colour = dir)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
  geom_text(data = wh_lab, aes(x = 1, y = 0, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3.2) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500), labels = comma) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = function(v) scales::percent(v, accuracy = 0.001, drop0trailing = TRUE),
                breaks = 10^(-6:0)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`At least k units shorter` = "#d95f02", `At least k units longer` = "#1f78b4"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Distance from the molecule's length, k (repeat units, log scale)", y = "Reads (log scale)",
       title = "How far reads are from their molecule") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(p_wh); save_plot(p_wh, file.path(plots_dir, "within_molecule_error_hist.png"), max(8, 4 * nrow(measures)), 4.8)
far <- wl[measure == primary, .(reads = .N, far_below = mean(dev < -10), far_above = mean(dev > 10)), by = file_stem]
rm(wl, rm_map)
timings["Within-molecule error"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

### Reads far from their molecule, per sample

Each point is one sample: the share of its reads (in kept molecules) whose `r primary` length is more than 10 units shorter, or more than 10 units longer, than their own molecule's length. These are the large PCR errors that collapsing removes: big slippage or deletion (shorter) and PCR chimeras or insertions (longer). It is a measure of PCR damage that needs no assumption about alleles. A sample far above the others had a harder PCR (more cycles, less template, or a long expanded allele), and its read-level results will be the most distorted.

```{r far_reads, fig.height=5}
far_l <- melt(far, id.vars = c("file_stem", "reads"), variable.name = "what", value.name = "share")
far_l[, what := factor(what, levels = c("far_below", "far_above"), labels = c("More than 10 units shorter", "More than 10 units longer"))]
p_far <- ggplot(far_l, aes(what, share)) + box_points_mean(digits = 1, percent = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads in the sample", title = "Reads far from their molecule's length, per sample") + theme_bw()
print(p_far); save_plot(p_far, file.path(plots_dir, "reads_far_from_molecule.png"), 8, 5)
```

## Molecules built from a longer template

Every molecule with at least `umi_min_reads` reads is checked against its own reads: a read counts as **long** if it is at least `umi_long_read_units` = `r params$umi_long_read_units` units longer than the molecule's `r primary` length. PCR mostly shortens reads, so a molecule should rarely hold reads much longer than itself. Where long reads make up at least `umi_long_read_share` = `r percent(params$umi_long_read_share)` of a molecule's reads, the molecule most likely came from a longer template whose reads were mostly shortened in PCR (an early-cycle deletion copied into most of the family), so the length it was given is too short. Such molecules are flagged, and `r if (isTRUE(params$umi_long_read_filter)) "**dropped** (umi_long_read_filter = TRUE): they are not in the molecule lengths used by Modules 5–7" else "**kept** (umi_long_read_filter = FALSE): they are counted in Modules 5–7 as they are"`. The check uses only the molecule's own reads, so nothing is assumed about alleles. All the plots in this section use every molecule with enough reads, before the filter.

### Flagged molecules by length and depth

**How to read this.** The x-axis is the molecule's `r primary` length (repeat units); the y-axis is the share of molecules at that length that are flagged. Each line is a band of reads per molecule. All samples are pooled; lengths with fewer than 20 molecules in a band are left out.

**What it shows.** Where the flagged molecules sit, and whether they are a problem of shallow molecules. A molecule with only a few reads is the easiest to get wrong: if a longer template's first copies were shortened, most of its few reads carry the shortened length. With more reads, the full-length reads become numerous enough for the length rule to find, so the flagged share should fall with depth. Lengths where shallow molecules are flagged far more often than deep ones are lengths where shallow molecules cannot be trusted. Even genuine molecules are sometimes flagged, because a single stray long read (a PCR chimera) is already a large share of a 3–5-read molecule; the flagged share at a common length shows that background.

```{r long_read_flag, fig.height=4.8}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
lf <- molecules[kept_depth == TRUE & !is.na(primary_length)]
lf_bw <- if (nrow(lf) && diff(stats::quantile(lf$primary_length, c(0.001, 0.999))) > 40) 5 else 1
d_edges <- unique(c(params$umi_min_reads, 6, 11, 21, 51, Inf))
d_edges <- d_edges[d_edges >= params$umi_min_reads]
d_lab <- vapply(seq_len(length(d_edges) - 1), function(i) if (is.infinite(d_edges[i + 1])) paste0(d_edges[i], "+ reads") else if (d_edges[i + 1] - 1 == d_edges[i]) paste(d_edges[i], "reads") else paste0(d_edges[i], "-", d_edges[i + 1] - 1, " reads"), "")
lf[, depth := cut(n_reads, d_edges, right = FALSE, labels = d_lab)]
lf[, length_bin := floor(primary_length / lf_bw) * lf_bw]
lf_bin <- lf[, .(molecules = .N, flagged = mean(long_flag)), by = .(depth, length_bin)][molecules >= 20]
if (nrow(lf_bin)) lf_bin <- lf_bin[lf_bin[, .(length_bin = seq(min(length_bin), max(length_bin), by = lf_bw)), by = depth], on = .(depth, length_bin)]
p_lf <- ggplot(lf_bin, aes(length_bin + (lf_bw - 1) / 2, flagged, colour = depth)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.9, name = "Reads per molecule") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = paste("Molecule", primary, "length (repeat units)"), y = "Molecules flagged",
       title = "Molecules flagged by the long-read check",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s of %s molecules with enough reads flagged (%s); flag = at least %s of reads %s+ units longer than the molecule",
                          comma(sum(lf$long_flag)), comma(nrow(lf)), percent(mean(lf$long_flag), 0.1), percent(params$umi_long_read_share), params$umi_long_read_units)) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(p_lf); save_plot(p_lf, file.path(plots_dir, "long_read_flag_by_length.png"), 10, 4.8)
long_tab <- lf[, .(molecules = .N, flagged = sum(long_flag), share_flagged = mean(long_flag)), by = .(depth, length_bin)][order(depth, length_bin)]
```

### Effect on the molecule length distribution

**How to read this.** The `r primary` length distribution of molecules for the whole run, each sample scaled to its own total and then averaged, so every sample counts equally. Four versions are drawn: every molecule with at least `r params$umi_min_reads` reads and no long-read filter; the same with the filter; and, for comparison, no filter but a higher `umi_min_reads` of 6 and of 11. The y-axis is square-root so that small shares stay visible.

**What it shows.** What the filter removes and whether it agrees with simply demanding more reads per molecule. If the molecules the filter removes are artefacts of shallow sampling, the filtered line should come close to the lines with more reads per molecule, while keeping the shallow molecules that show no sign of a longer template.

```{r long_read_dist, fig.height=4.8}
lf_lim <- stats::quantile(lf$primary_length, 0.999)
lv <- rbindlist(list(
  lf[, .(version = "No filter", file_stem, len = round(primary_length))],
  lf[long_flag == FALSE, .(version = "Long-read filter", file_stem, len = round(primary_length))],
  lf[n_reads >= max(6, params$umi_min_reads), .(version = sprintf("No filter, at least %d reads", max(6, params$umi_min_reads)), file_stem, len = round(primary_length))],
  lf[n_reads >= max(11, params$umi_min_reads), .(version = sprintf("No filter, at least %d reads", max(11, params$umi_min_reads)), file_stem, len = round(primary_length))]))
lv <- lv[len <= lf_lim, .N, by = .(version, file_stem, len)][, share := N / sum(N), by = .(version, file_stem)]
lv <- lv[, .(share = sum(share) / uniqueN(lf$file_stem)), by = .(version, len)]
lv[, version := factor(version, levels = unique(version))]
p_lv <- ggplot(lv, aes(len, share, colour = version)) + geom_step(direction = "mid", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("grey55", "#00838f", "#e6862e", "#7b3294"), levels(lv$version)), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_sqrt(labels = pct_axis()) +
  labs(x = paste(primary, "length (repeat units)"), y = "Share of molecules, averaged over samples\n(square-root axis)",
       title = "Molecule length distribution with and without the long-read filter") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(p_lv); save_plot(p_lv, file.path(plots_dir, "long_read_filter_distribution.png"), 10, 4.8)
```

### Molecules flagged per sample

Each point is one sample: the share of its molecules (with enough reads) that the long-read check flags. A sample far above the others had more PCR damage, so more of its molecules were built from shortened copies; `r if (isTRUE(params$umi_long_read_filter)) "with the filter on, it also loses more molecules" else "with the filter off, its molecule results are the most affected"`.

```{r long_read_sample, fig.height=4.5}
lf_s <- lf[, .(molecules = .N, flagged = sum(long_flag), share_flagged = mean(long_flag)), by = file_stem]
p_lfs <- ggplot(lf_s, aes("", share_flagged)) + box_points_mean(digits = 1, percent = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Molecules flagged", title = "Molecules flagged by the long-read check, per sample") + theme_bw()
print(p_lfs); save_plot(p_lfs, file.path(plots_dir, "long_read_flag_per_sample.png"), 6, 4.5)
dt_full(lf_s, caption = "Molecules flagged by the long-read check, per sample", digits = 3)
timings["Long-read check"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Choosing a molecule's length

Every molecule (UMI family) is given one `r primary` length, made from its own reads by a *length rule* (`umi_collapse_stat`). The rule used in this run is **`r used_rule_text`**. Duke calculates every rule below for every molecule, so their effect can be compared; none of them uses alleles or any other molecule.

- **top_cluster, `r params$umi_top_cluster_k` reads**: the longest length that at least `r params$umi_top_cluster_k` reads agree on, within a window that widens with length (± `r params$umi_top_cluster_w` + `r params$umi_top_cluster_wfrac` × length). PCR slippage mostly shortens reads, so the longest well-supported length is the best guess at the template.
- **`r rules_md$top_cluster_share$label`**: the same, but the agreeing reads must also be at least `r paste0(signif(100 * rules_md$top_cluster_share$share, 3), "%")` of the molecule's reads (`umi_top_cluster_min_share`; 20% by default), so a few stray long reads (PCR chimeras) cannot set the length of a large molecule.
- **longest length on `r params$umi_top_cluster_k` reads**: the longest exact length held by at least `r params$umi_top_cluster_k` reads (no window).
- **mode**, **median**, **mean**: the commonest, middle and average read length. They follow the majority of reads, so slipped reads pull them down.

### How well each rule behaves

**How to read this.** Three tests of each rule, made on the molecules' own reads (a random subset of up to 3,000 molecules), with no assumption about alleles. In every test **0 is perfect and a shorter bar is better**; the rule used in this run is drawn in orange and labelled "(used)", and the best rule in each test has its value in bold.

- **Agreement between halves** (units; lower is better): each molecule's reads are split at random into two halves and each half is collapsed; the bar is the average difference between the two lengths (molecules with at least 6 reads). A rule that a few reads can move gives two different answers.
- **Dependence on depth** (units; closer to 0 is better, in either direction): the length from 20 of a molecule's reads minus the length from 3 of them, averaged over molecules with at least 20 reads. Above 0 means the rule gives longer lengths when a molecule has more reads; below 0, shorter. A rule whose answer changes with depth makes deeply and shallowly sequenced samples incomparable.
- **Moved by stray reads** (% of molecules; lower is better): stray reads (10% of the molecule's reads, at least one) are borrowed from a random other molecule of the same sample, as a PCR chimera would add them, and the molecule is collapsed again; the bar is the share of molecules whose length moves by more than 2 units.

**What it shows.** Which rule gives the most stable length. A rule can do well on one test and badly on another: the median is hard to move with stray reads but is pulled down by slippage and drifts with depth; the plain top_cluster resists slippage but can be moved by a few stray long reads.

```{r collapse_scorecard, fig.height=4.5}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
rules <- collapse_rules(params)
rule_labels <- vapply(rules, `[[`, "", "label")
used_key <- if (params$umi_collapse_stat == "top_cluster") {
  if (params$umi_top_cluster_min_share == 0) "top_cluster_k" else "top_cluster_share"
} else params$umi_collapse_stat
rd_sc <- umi_reads[!is.na(molecule_id) & !is.na(primary) & molecule_id %in% molecules[kept == TRUE, molecule_id], .(file_stem, molecule_id, length = primary)]
scorecard <- collapse_scorecard(rd_sc, rules)
rm(rd_sc)
scorecard[, shown := ifelse(!is.na(used_key) & rule == used_key, paste(label, "(used)"), label)]
sc_l <- melt(scorecard, id.vars = c("rule", "shown"), measure.vars = c("split_half", "depth_drift", "chimera_shift"), variable.name = "test", value.name = "value")
sc_l[, test := factor(test, levels = c("split_half", "depth_drift", "chimera_shift"),
                      labels = c("Agreement between halves\n(mean difference, units)\nlower is better",
                                 "Dependence on depth\n(20 reads minus 3, mean, units)\ncloser to 0 is better",
                                 "Moved by stray reads\n(% of molecules moved > 2 units)\nlower is better"))]
sc_l[, shown := factor(shown, levels = rev(scorecard$shown))]
sc_l[, is_used := !is.na(used_key) & rule == used_key]
# The stray-read test is a share: drawn in percent, so its axis can carry the % sign
sc_l[grepl("stray", test), value := 100 * value]
sc_l[, best := abs(value) == min(abs(value)), by = test]
sc_l[, lab := ifelse(grepl("stray", test), paste0(formatC(value, format = "f", digits = 1), "%"), formatC(value, format = "f", digits = 2))]
p_sc <- ggplot(sc_l, aes(value, shown)) + geom_col(aes(fill = is_used), width = 0.6) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab, hjust = ifelse(value < 0, 1.15, -0.15), fontface = ifelse(best, "bold", "plain")), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ test, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#d95f02", `FALSE` = "#00838f"), labels = c(`TRUE` = "Rule used in this run", `FALSE` = "Other rules"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.3, 0.3))) +
  labs(x = "0 is perfect; bold = best rule in that test", y = NULL, title = "How each length rule behaves",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s molecules tested for halves and stray reads, %s for depth", comma(scorecard$n_split_half[1]), comma(scorecard$n_depth_drift[1]))) +
  theme_bw() + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 9), legend.position = "bottom")
print(p_sc); save_plot(p_sc, file.path(plots_dir, "length_rule_scorecard.png"), 12, 5)
sc_tab <- scorecard[, .(rule = label, used = ifelse(!is.na(used_key) & rule == used_key, "yes", ""),
                        `halves: mean difference (units, lower better)` = split_half,
                        `depth: 20 reads minus 3 (units, closer to 0 better)` = depth_drift,
                        `stray reads: % moved > 2 units (lower better)` = 100 * chimera_shift,
                        `molecules (halves, stray reads)` = n_split_half, `molecules (depth)` = n_depth_drift)]
dt_compact(sc_tab, caption = "Length rule tests: 0 is perfect in every test; the rule used in this run is marked", digits = 2)
```

### Where the rules differ

**How to read this.** Every rule is compared with the rule used in this run (**`r used_rule_text`**), which is the reference and so has no line of its own. The x-axis is each molecule's length under the rule used; the y-axis is the share of molecules at that length that each other rule would make more than 2 units **shorter** (left) or **longer** (right). A line along zero means that rule agrees with the one used. The table gives the totals over all molecules, with the rule used as a row of zeros for reference.

**What it shows.** Most molecules get the same length whichever rule is used; the differences sit at particular lengths, typically just above a common length (where a few stray long reads can set a molecule's length) and below it (where slipped reads pull the mode, median and mean down).

```{r collapse_compare, fig.height=5}
used <- molecule_lengths[measure == primary, .(molecule_id, used = length)]
cmp <- used[collapse_compare, on = "molecule_id", nomatch = NULL]
bw_cc <- if (diff(stats::quantile(cmp$used, c(0.001, 0.999), na.rm = TRUE)) > 40) 5 else 1
cmp[, length_bin := floor(used / bw_cc) * bw_cc]
rules_shown <- setdiff(names(rules), used_key)
cl <- rbindlist(lapply(rules_shown, function(r) {
  cmp[, .(rule = rule_labels[[r]], molecules = .N, shorter = mean(get(r) - used < -2, na.rm = TRUE), longer = mean(get(r) - used > 2, na.rm = TRUE)), by = length_bin]
}))[molecules >= 20]
# Lengths with too few molecules are drawn as gaps, so lines do not join distant lengths
cl <- cl[cl[, .(length_bin = seq(min(length_bin), max(length_bin), by = bw_cc)), by = rule], on = .(rule, length_bin)]
cl_l <- melt(cl, id.vars = c("rule", "length_bin", "molecules"), measure.vars = c("shorter", "longer"), variable.name = "direction", value.name = "share")
cl_l[, direction := factor(direction, levels = c("shorter", "longer"), labels = c("More than 2 units shorter than the rule used", "More than 2 units longer than the rule used"))]
cl_l[, rule := factor(rule, levels = rule_labels)]
# One fixed colour per rule, so the same rule has the same colour whichever rule is used
rule_cols <- c(top_cluster_k = "#1f78b4", top_cluster_share = "#d95f02", max_supported = "#33a02c",
               mode = "#6a3d9a", median = "grey40", mean = "#e7298a")[names(rules)]
names(rule_cols) <- rule_labels
p_cc <- ggplot(cl_l, aes(length_bin + (bw_cc - 1) / 2, share, colour = rule)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ direction, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = rule_cols, name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = paste("Molecule", primary, "length under the rule used (repeat units)"), y = "Molecules at that length",
       title = "Where each length rule would change molecules",
       subtitle = paste0("Each line compared with the rule used in this run: ", used_rule_text)) + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(p_cc); save_plot(p_cc, file.path(plots_dir, "length_rule_comparison.png"), 11, 5)
rule_tab <- rbindlist(lapply(names(rules), function(r) {
  d <- cmp[[r]] - cmp$used
  data.table(rule = paste0(rule_labels[[r]], if (identical(r, used_key)) " (used, reference)" else ""), molecules = sum(is.finite(d)), shorter_by_more_than_2 = mean(d < -2, na.rm = TRUE),
             longer_by_more_than_2 = mean(d > 2, na.rm = TRUE), median_difference = stats::median(d, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
dt_compact(rule_tab, caption = paste0("Molecule length by each rule compared with the rule used in this run (", used_rule_text, "), all molecules: share made more than 2 units shorter or longer, and median difference in units"), digits = 3)
timings["Length rules"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Read and molecule distributions

The `r primary` length distribution of reads (grey) and of molecules (teal) for the whole run: each sample's distribution is scaled to its own total and then averaged, so every sample counts equally whatever its depth. The y-axis is square-root so that a minor allele is visible next to the major one, and the x-axis stops at the length that 99.9% of molecules fall below. Collapsing should narrow each allele's peak and remove the stutter shoulder below it. One sample is shown below as an example; every sample is in `plots/reads_vs_molecules/`.

```{r dist_compare, fig.height=4.5}
dc <- rbind(lengths[measure == primary, .(file_stem, unit = "Reads", length)],
            molecule_lengths[measure == primary, .(file_stem, unit = "Molecules", length)])
dc <- dc[, .N, by = .(file_stem, unit, length = floor(length + 0.5))][, prop := N / sum(N), by = .(file_stem, unit)]
# Lengths with no reads or molecules are drawn as zero, so the step line drops between peaks
dc <- dc[dc[, .(length = seq(min(length), max(length))), by = .(file_stem, unit)], on = .(file_stem, unit, length)]
dc[is.na(prop), `:=`(N = 0L, prop = 0)]
xmax_all <- stats::quantile(molecule_lengths[measure == primary, length], 0.999, na.rm = TRUE) + 10
grid <- CJ(file_stem = unique(dc$file_stem), unit = c("Reads", "Molecules"), length = seq(0, ceiling(xmax_all)))
cohort <- dc[grid, on = .(file_stem, unit, length)][is.na(prop), prop := 0][, .(prop = mean(prop)), by = .(unit, length)]
p_cohort <- ggplot(cohort, aes(length, prop, colour = unit)) + geom_step(direction = "mid") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Reads = "grey55", Molecules = "#00838f"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "sqrt", labels = pct_axis()) +
  labs(x = paste(primary, "length"), y = "Share, averaged over samples (square-root axis)",
       title = "Repeat length, reads against molecules: whole run", subtitle = sprintf("%d samples, each weighted equally", uniqueN(dc$file_stem))) + theme_bw()
print(p_cohort); save_plot(p_cohort, file.path(plots_dir, "reads_vs_molecules_cohort.png"), 10, 4.5)

xmax <- molecule_lengths[measure == primary, .(xmax = stats::quantile(length, 0.999, na.rm = TRUE) + 10), by = file_stem]
dc <- xmax[dc, on = "file_stem"][length <= xmax]
draw_dc <- function(d, title) ggplot(d, aes(length, prop, colour = unit)) + geom_step(direction = "mid") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Reads = "grey55", Molecules = "#00838f"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "sqrt", labels = pct_axis()) +
  labs(x = paste(primary, "length"), y = "Share of reads or molecules (square-root axis)", title = title) + theme_bw()
first <- unique(dc$file_stem)[1]
p_dc <- draw_dc(dc[file_stem == first], paste("Example sample:", first))
print(p_dc)
if (params$plot_per_sample) for (s in unique(dc$file_stem))
  save_plot(draw_dc(dc[file_stem == s], s), file.path(plots_dir, "reads_vs_molecules", paste0(s, ".png")), 9, 4.5)
```

# Save output

```{r save}
mol_dir <- file.path(umi_dir, "molecules"); dir.create(mol_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
wide <- dcast(molecule_lengths, file_stem + molecule_id ~ measure, value.var = "length")
wide <- molecules[kept == TRUE, .(file_stem, molecule_id, umi, n_reads)][wide, on = .(file_stem, molecule_id)]
for (s in unique(wide$file_stem)) fwrite(wide[file_stem == s], file.path(mol_dir, paste0(s, ".tsv.gz")), sep = "\t")
module4_output <- list(umi_reads = umi_reads, molecules = molecules, molecule_lengths = molecule_lengths,
                       clustering = clustering, summary = summary_tab, collapse_compare = collapse_compare, hash = params$module_hash)
output_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "04_umi.RData")
save(module4_output, file = output_path)
write_excel_function(list(summary = summary_tab, extraction = dcast(outcome, file_stem ~ umi_outcome, value.var = "N", fill = 0),
                          within_molecule_error = we_sum, within_error_by_length = we_len, reads_far_from_molecule = far,
                          long_read_flag_by_length = long_tab, long_read_flag_per_sample = lf_s, length_rule_scorecard = scorecard, length_rule_comparison = rule_tab), xlsx_path)
```

**`r comma(sum(molecules$kept))`** molecules kept across **`r uniqueN(molecules$file_stem)`** samples.
